steps.what: Read the relevant energy conservation measure guidance
Explain energy conservation measures and answer household questions

tasks.design: Group existing measure guidance by household question in {DOCS}. The technician checks applicability and explains the measures directly; no generated financial promise or new visit record is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measure sheets are scattered and difficult to locate during a visit.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document search and topic links are enough for common questions.
tasks.still_hard: Actual savings depend on the dwelling and behaviour, and practical suitability needs discussion.
tasks.human_edge: Show how to use the measure and discover why the household may struggle with it.

ambition.what: Use the recovered lookup time to explain options to household members who need a demonstration.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a curated measure library can shorten document navigation while suitability and practical explanation remain human work.

assumptions: Boundary is a spoken explanation during a visit, including the actual guidance lookup. No educational follow-up report or consent log is assumed to exist today.

The operator's technical lead maintains measure name, applicability, cautions, guidance date and any supported calculation assumptions. The technician reads original sheets where metadata are absent. No new structured capture is priced as today's work.
Native topic links remove five units of search from twenty; fifteen units of reading and applicability checking remain. Existing calculation or search runtime earns no saving.
The illustrative shares are not measured organisation data.
unknowns: Whether guides are already immediately accessible
research_questions: Does grouping the existing sheets save navigation without encouraging unsupported savings claims?

already_counted.description: Read the actual guidance and explain suitability and use

incremental.description: Maintain topic links and withdraw superseded sheets

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver checked weatherization bids

steps.what: Read weatherization survey quantities, scope and approved rates for the bid
Prepare bid quantity and price tables from checked weatherization inputs
Prepare the written weatherization scope, exclusions and technical explanation

loop.input: Checked survey facts and approved scope clauses
loop.output: Scope narrative linked to source observations
loop.check: Technician checks each proposed measure, exclusion and explanation against the actual survey and removes unsupported savings claims
loop.stop: Missing observations, conflicting scope or unapproved terms stop generation for manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured fields fill the price table but cannot express every observed building constraint

steps.what: Check the final weatherization bid and authorize its exact customer delivery
Send the exact authorized weatherization bid to the customer
Save the written bid in the existing job document folder

tasks.design: Fill price and quantity tables in {DOCS} from the checked {OPS_SYSTEM} survey record, using native templates before custom integration. A bounded narrative draft receives full technical review, and {EMAIL} sends only the final authorized snapshot to the checked address.
tasks.previous_blocker: Survey facts and rate tables are copied into bid documents and job-specific explanations are written repeatedly.
tasks.enabler_now: Deterministic merge fields handle prices and quantities; a small checked drafting loop handles irregular technical prose.
tasks.still_hard: The technician must establish the actual building condition and whether each proposed measure is appropriate.
tasks.human_edge: Take responsibility for scope, exclusions and achievable work rather than accepting plausible prose.

ambition.what: Present a separately priced alternative measure package when the survey supports one.

reach.task: Explain the observed constraints behind a proposed measure
reach.learn: Survey interpretation and limits of savings estimates

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: survey-field merges and rate arithmetic can generate bid tables; job-specific prose needs source-based review before customer delivery.

assumptions: Representative boundary is a technician-authored bid using an existing completed survey, ending at actual customer delivery and ordinary filing. Written technical reports use the same source and review principle; issuing a statutory label or signing a contract is a separate authorized act, not automated here.

Surveying staff produce job id, measured area, quantities, measure codes and observed constraints in the normal site-survey workflow. The estimator maintains rate version and approved clauses. s1 counts checking and manual extraction where fields are missing; upkeep funds failed merge repair.

This case assumes the technician already has delegated authority to deliver standard bids within approved rates. If delivery authority lies elsewhere, that existing review and labour must be mapped before use; no fictional self-approval or new supervisor is added.
s4 reviews a complete final bid and its destination for real delivery. Changed prices, wording, scope, attachments or recipient void authorization. s6 is an ungated ordinary save with no saving.
Native table generation or mail delivery already present earns no new labour benefit. The send is a real composed customer delivery, not a renamed same-system save.
unknowns: Which bid fields are actually retyped today
How often survey records need manual extraction
research_questions: Do generated bids preserve every exclusion and rate version?
How many irregular records require manual table or narrative repair?

already_counted.description: Read actual survey inputs, review the narrative and final delivery snapshot, and save the bid

incremental.description: Repair failed merges and delivery exceptions, maintain rates, clauses and drafting checks

approvals.approved_version: Final bid snapshot with exact scope, prices, clauses, attachments and checked recipient from s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R57 gross43 minus upkeep5 gives38. With a scanned survey and no applicable narrative template, table work retains20 of25 and narrative32 of35; source20, final review15 and save1 remain. R88 gross12 minus upkeep5 gives7, including only the real four-unit delivery saving.
